To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
3T 3‐F442 cells are highly sensitive to rat GH only for a few days after confluence and that the mRNA for glycerophosphate‐dehydrogenase is translated immediately after synthesis.
the sensitivity of F442A preadipocytes to growth hormone declines after confluence and that this decrease is not due to exhaustion but is a specific property of the cells.
the 3T3 preadipose cells are able to differentiate into adipocytes and that growth hormone induces this conversion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the mechanism of the conversion of preadipocytes into adipose cells and of the role played by growth hormone.
the regulation of the differentiation of 3T3 fibroblasts and the mechanism by which growth hormone induces this conversion.
the mechanism by which growth hormone induces adipogenesis in 3T3 preadipose cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the sensitivity of F442A preadipose cells to rat growth hormone is limited to a short time period after confluence, and that this hormone is a potent inducer of the synthesis of glycerophosphade dehydrogenase mRNA and of the activity of the enzyme.
the F442A cells are sensitive to rat growth hormones only at confluence and that the sensitivity is lost after 3 days.

the growth hormone‐induced differentiation in preadipose cells is a multistep process which involves at least three different phases: the induction of the differentiation process by growth hormone, the induction of glycosyltransferase and the induction of glycolytic and lipogenic enzymes, including glycerophosphate acyltransferase and glycerophosphate dihydrogenase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
growth hormone‐induced glycerophosphate‐dehydrogenase mRNA is synthesized at confluence and translated within a short period after its synthesis.
F442A cells become sensitive to rat growth factor at confluence but only for a short period of time.

growth hormone induces the synthesis of the enzyme glycerophosphate‐dehydrogenase in preadipose cells, and that the hormone‐induced synthesis of the enzyme requires the synthesis of the mRNA for this enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the growth hormone is able to induce the expression of glycerophosphade dehydrogenase at a very specific time in the cell cycle.
the sensitivity of the cells to the hormone is a very important factor in the regulation of the hormone's effects.

the sensitivity of preadipocytes to GH declines rapidly after reaching confluence and that the induction of glycolysis and lipogenesis occurs at the same time as the mRNA for the key enzyme, glycerophosphate‐dehydrogenase, is detected.
